A very intriguing topic! As a Linux system administrator, I must tell you that APT32 OceanLotus, also known as Ocean Bunyip, is a notorious cyber espionage group believed to be sponsored by the Vietnamese government.

 OceanLotus gained notoriety for its sophisticated and stealthy operations, often targeting high-value targets in Southeast Asia, particularly Vietnam. Their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) have been observed to be highly advanced, evading detection and making them a challenging threat to track.

From a technical standpoint, OceanLotus is known to employ various malware families, including the OceanBark and OceanDart variants, which are designed to evade detection and maintain persistence on compromised systems. These malware families are capable of conducting reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and even remote control of compromised systems.

In terms of their targeting, OceanLotus has been observed to focus on high-profile targets, including government officials, military personnel, and influential business leaders in Vietnam. Their methods of operation often involve spear phishing, exploiting vulnerabilities in software, and using social engineering tactics to gain access to sensitive systems.
